title: GeoVersa: Design-Based Residual-Correction Forests for Digital Soil Mapping
description: GeoVersa ships DB-TARF (Design-Based Targeted Adaptive Residual Forest), a random forest augmented by a cross-fitted, out-of-fold-selected residual correction (residual forests, Cubist, ordinary kriging, MLP, and a variogram-informed radial-basis smoother), together with design-based conformal prediction intervals. It extends the Wadoux et al. (2021) design-based paradigm from point accuracy (RMSE) to interval coverage (PICP). Benchmarked on the public materials of Wadoux et al. (2021): above-ground live woody biomass (Baccini et al. 2012) over a 928 km x 1642 km Amazonian rectangle at 1 km resolution, with calibration samples of n=500 under random, regular-grid and clustered designs. The repository also preserves the ConvKrigingNet2D research line — a hybrid deep architecture fusing a 2D CNN raster-patch encoder, a tabular MLP, and a coordinate MLP through a differentiable anisotropic residual kriging layer.
notes: The DB-TARF core is published on CRAN as the GeoVersa R package (v0.3.0, 2026-07-06). The ConvKrigingNet2D deep-kriging code is research code kept in the repository and is not part of the CRAN package. Benchmark uses the Wadoux et al. (2021) design-based validation framework.
